title: The Middle Class and Vulnerability to Income Poverty: Implications for Social Protection in the Philippines
authors: Cabalfin, D.L.D.; Albert, J.R.G.; Mahmoud, M.A.
tldr: Vulnerability to income poverty affects 30% of Filipino households, far exceeding official poverty, demanding broader social protection beyond current poverty-targeted programs.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional poverty measures are static and underestimate the at-risk population, failing to capture households at risk of downward mobility due to economic shocks. Understanding the dynamics and sources of vulnerability is critical as the Philippines aspires to become a predominantly middle-class society by 2040.
approach: Used merged FIES-LFS data from 2018, 2021, and 2023 covering 147,717 to 165,029 households per survey round.
Applied the Chaudhuri and Datt (2001) methodology to estimate household vulnerability as the probability of being income-poor in the next period.
Modeled log per capita household income as a function of observable household characteristics and community-level covariates.
Estimated model parameters using a three-step feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) procedure.
Constructed provincial communications and waterworks infrastructure indices.
Incorporated monthly average rainfall shocks from 48 PAGASA weather stations.
Cross-validated results by comparing predicted vulnerability-based poverty rates against observed poverty incidence.
Decomposed vulnerability sources into high-volatility-of-income and low-mean-income categories.
findings: num: 30.0% of Filipino households are vulnerable to poverty, 2.75 times higher than the 10.9% poverty incidence in 2023.
num: 86% of vulnerable households experience high income volatility, while 14% have persistently low mean income.
num: Rural vulnerability is 43.0% versus 20.0% urban in 2023.
num: Regional vulnerability ranges from 9.0% in NCR to 76.0% in rural BARMM.
num: 44% of low-income but non-poor households face significant vulnerability risk.
num: 21-24% of non-poor households are assessed as vulnerable to falling into poverty.
num: Philippines' social protection effective coverage is only 34.9%, far below the 71.2% upper-middle income country average.
Agriculture is the highest-risk sector with 25% poverty rate and 60% vulnerability rate in 2023.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Updated empirical profile of the Philippine middle-income class and its vulnerability to income poverty using the latest available FIES-LFS data spanning the COVID-19 pandemic. Decomposes vulnerability sources into income volatility and low mean income components.
directly_justifies: Vulnerability affects 30.0% of Filipino households, 2.75 times higher than observed poverty.
86% of vulnerable families experience income volatility.
Rural vulnerability incidence is 43.0% versus 20.0% urban.
Regional vulnerability ranges from 9.0% in NCR to 76.0% in rural BARMM.
Philippines' social protection effective coverage is only 34.9% versus the upper-middle income average of 71.2%.
limits: Uses cross-sectional data rather than longitudinal panel data.
Rules out aggregate shocks or structural changes.

limitations: Uses cross-sectional data rather than longitudinal panel data.
Rules out aggregate shocks or structural changes per the Chaudhuri (2001) assumption.
Vulnerability estimate does not capture long-term economic prospects or intergenerational mobility.
Cross-sectional approach may underestimate true vulnerability.
Analysis relies on self-reported household income data subject to measurement error.
remember_this: Vulnerability to poverty affects 30% of Filipino households, far exceeding the 10.9% official poverty rate.
Most vulnerable households face income volatility rather than persistently low incomes.
Rural and BARMM households face disproportionately higher vulnerability than urban and NCR households.
Social protection coverage in the Philippines lags significantly behind upper-middle income country standards.
Education and formal employment are strong protective factors against household vulnerability.
